unit.title: Homophones, Paronyms & Spelling Traps
unit.subtitle: haya/halla, echo/hecho, sino/si no, porque/por qué and friends

grammar.title: The spelling traps that catch even natives
grammar.intro: At C2, listening is easy; spelling is where mastery shows. Spanish is full of words that sound identical but mean utterly different things — haya/halla, echo/hecho, tuvo/tubo, valla/vaya/baya — and of splits that hinge on a single space or accent: sino vs si no, the porque family, también vs tan bien. Get these right and your written Spanish reads as fully native.

sections.heading: Same sound, different word (h and b/v)
sections.body: Haya is from haber (subjunctive) or the beech tree; halla is from hallar (to find); aya is a nanny; allá means “over there”. Echo is from echar (to throw/put); hecho is from hacer (done) or “a fact”. Tuvo is from tener; tubo is a pipe. Valla is a fence/hurdle; vaya is from ir; baya is a berry.
conj: echar → I throw / hacer → done, fact

ex.es: Espero que haya terminado antes de que la policía lo halle.
ex.en: I hope he has finished before the police find him.

ex.es: Te echo de menos desde que se ha hecho de noche.
ex.en: I miss you now that night has fallen.

sections.heading: sino vs si no
sections.body: Sino (one word) is a conjunction of contrast, “but rather”, and also a noun meaning “fate”. Si no (two words) is the conditional si + negation, “if not / unless”. Test: if you can insert a verb or “entonces” after it, it's the two-word si no.

ex.es: No lo hizo por dinero, sino por orgullo.
ex.en: He didn't do it for money, but out of pride.

ex.es: Avísame; si no, me marcho sin ti.
ex.en: Let me know; if not, I'm leaving without you.

sections.heading: The porque family
sections.body: Four forms, four jobs. ¿Por qué? (two words, accent) asks “why?”. Porque (one word) answers “because”. El porqué (one word, accent) is the noun “the reason”. Por que (two words, no accent) is the rarer “for which / for … to”, where que is a relative or por is demanded by a verb (preocuparse por que…).

ex.en: Why are you silent? — Because I don't want to argue.

ex.es: Nunca entendí el porqué de su enfado.
ex.en: I never understood the reason for his anger.

sections.heading: a ver/haber · asimismo/así mismo · también/tan bien
sections.body: A ver (a + the verb ver) means “let's see”; haber is the auxiliary/infinitive. Asimismo (one word) means “likewise, also”; así mismo (two words) means “in that very way / right there”. También (one word) means “also”; tan bien (two words) means “so well”.
conj: in that very manner / right there

ex.en: Let's see whether he should have warned us earlier.

ex.es: Canta tan bien que yo también quiero aprender.
ex.en: She sings so well that I want to learn too.

takeaways: haya = haber/tree · halla = hallar · aya = nanny · allá = over there.
echo = echar · hecho = hacer/fact; tuvo = tener · tubo = pipe; valla = fence · vaya = ir · baya = berry.
sino = 'but rather'/fate; si no = 'if not'. porque (because) / ¿por qué? (why) / el porqué (the reason) / por que (for which).
a ver ≠ haber; también (also) ≠ tan bien (so well); asimismo (likewise) ≠ así mismo (in that very way).

mistakes.w: No fue culpa suya, si no del sistema.
mistakes.r: No fue culpa suya, sino del sistema.
mistakes.why: This is contrast ('not X but Y'), so it's the one-word conjunction 'sino', not the conditional 'si no'.
The auxiliary of haber is 'haya'; 'halla' is from hallar (to find).

mistakes.r: No sé por qué lo dijo.
mistakes.why: An indirect question uses two words with an accent: 'por qué'. 'Porqué' (one word) is only the noun 'the reason'.

exercises.prompt: Espero que ___ estudiado lo suficiente para el examen.
exercises.prompt_en: I hope you've studied enough for the exam.
exercises.no: The auxiliary (haber) is “hayas”; “hallas” is from hallar (you find).

exercises.prompt: No lo hice por interés, ___ por convicción.
exercises.prompt_en: I didn't do it out of self-interest, but out of conviction.
exercises.no: This is contrast ('not X but Y'), so it's the one-word conjunction “sino”.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I never understood the reason for his anger."
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! El sustantivo 'el porqué' (una palabra, con tilde).
exercises.no: The noun 'the reason' is “el porqué” — one word with an accent.

exercises.prompt: Se le rompió un ___ del fregadero y el agua salió a chorros. (pipe)
exercises.prompt_en: A pipe under the sink broke and water gushed out.
exercises.hint: A pipe — spelled with b, not from 'tener'.
exercises.no: A pipe is “tubo” (with b); “tuvo” is from tener.

exercises.prompt: Match each homophone to its meaning.

exercises.tts: A ver si debería haber avisado antes.
accepted: a ver si deberia haber avisado antes
exercises.translation: Let's see whether he should have warned us earlier.
exercises.no: It was: “A ver si debería haber avisado antes.” (a ver = let's see; haber = auxiliary).

exercises.scenario: A friend proofreads your message and questions a word 🔍

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.es: Escribiste “canta tan bien que yo también quiero aprender”. ¿No es todo con “también”?
lines.en: You wrote “canta tan bien que yo también quiero aprender”. Isn't it all with “también”?

options.text: No: “tan bien” (dos palabras) es 'so well', y “también” (una) es 'also'. Cada uno está en su sitio.
Tienes razón, debería ser “canta también que yo también quiero aprender”.
Da igual, “tan bien” y “también” significan exactamente lo mismo.

exercises.no: “tan bien” (two words) means 'so well' and “también” (one) means 'also' — both are correct as written, option a.

exercises.say: No fue por dinero, sino por orgullo, aunque nadie entienda el porqué.
exercises.en: It wasn't for money, but out of pride, though nobody understands the reason.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “No fue por dinero, sino por orgullo, aunque nadie entienda el porqué.”
